div.head: Had 11
div.ab: And wise wæran worldwitan, þe to godcundan rihtlagan þas laga setton, folce for steore, ⁊ halidóm ⁊ hadas for Godes lufan wurðodon ⁊ Godes hus ⁊ Godes þeowas deoplice griðedon.
⁊ wíse wæron woruldwitan, þe to godcundan rihtlagan þas lage setton, folce for steore, ⁊ halidom ⁊ hadas for Godes lufon wurðedon ⁊ Godes hus ⁊ Godes þeowas deopplice gryðedon.
And wise wæran worldwitan þe to godcundan rihtlagan þas laga setton folce for steore, and halidom and hadas for Godes lufan wurðodon and Godes hus and Godes þeowas deoplice griðedon.

(Und weise waren die Staatsregenten, welche zu geistlichen Rechtsgesetzen diese Gesetze aufstellten, dem Volke zur Zucht, und aus Liebe zu Gott Heiligthum und Ordines ehrten und Gotteshäuser und Gottesdiener mit hohem Sonderfrieden privilegirten fehlt hq.)

And wise were the secular counsellors who added these laws to the spiritual laws, for the discipline of the people, and out of love for God honoured holy things and orders, and privileged God's houses and God's servants with high special peace.

And the secular councillors were wise who added to the ecclesiastical right laws these laws for the control of the people, and honoured relics and holy orders for the love of God, and greatly privileged God’s houses and God’s servants.

And wise were the councilors who added these laws to the ecclesiastical canons for the guidance of the people, and who venerated the sacraments and holy orders for the love of God, and greatly honored God’s house and God’s servants.

div.note: This clause is lacking in hq (so not in H, as K says); Liebermann thinks it perhaps better, since it agrees word for word with Grið 24 and partly in content with Had 1.1 and 1.3. The OE in N is from D. In D, ‘Incipit de baptismo’ (Napier, Wulfstan IV) follows; O ends here. Liebermann compares VIII Atr 36 and Grið 24.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘And the secular councillors were wise who added to the ecclesiastical right laws these laws for the control of people, and honoured relics and holy orders for the love of God, and greatly privileged God's houses and God's servants.’).; AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 20 / 21, October 2026 (was “re-edits”, now “reedits”)
And . . . griðedon: omitted H, text supplied from D

Textus Roffensis inverts clauses 9.1 and 10 and omits clause 11 entirely. This is in keeping with the scribe’s treatment of The Compilation on Status generally, which he disarticulates and reedits in order to reformulate the component texts for a twelfth-century readership and fit them into the manuscript’s organizational program. The preterite verb tenses of this clause recall those of On the Ranks of People and Law, thus providing a neat bookend to the Compilation.

Ferner als Atr oder Grið steht dem Texte EGu Pro 2. Wisc woroldwitan als Gesetzgeber erwähnt auch VI Atr 51.—Der Satz mit dem späten Verb griðian (s. o. 1, 1²) gehört vielleicht nicht ursprünglich zu Had. Er stammt wahrscheinlich aus derselben Quelle wie Grið 24; denn letztere Stelle schöpfte nicht aus Had allein, da sie zu VIII Atr 36 näher steht mit dem Worte woroldlaga. Anderseits kann Had nicht aus Grið fliessen, weil letztere Quelle allein die Atr fremden Wörter on geardagum einführt

EGu Pro 2 is further from the text than Atr or Grið. Wisc woroldwitan as lawgivers are also mentioned in VI Atr 51. — The sentence with the late verb griðian (see above 1, 1²) perhaps did not originally belong to Had. It probably comes from the same source as Grið 24; for the latter passage did not draw on Had alone, since with the word woroldlaga it stands closer to VIII Atr 36. On the other hand Had cannot derive from Grið, because the latter source alone introduces the words on geardagum, foreign to Atr
